_comment: temper-constraints's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
wasm_expected_failures.json (temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json,
wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json, wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json,
wasm_expected_failures_design_bundle.json, wasm_expected_failures_constraint_compiler.json,
wasm_expected_failures_quality_oracle.json, wasm_expected_failures_io_types.json and
wasm_expected_failures_pcl_ir.json. Same contract -- see wasm_expected_failures.json's
_comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
It is a separate file rather than more entries in a shared one because run_wasm_tests.mjs
exits non-zero on an ORPHAN EXCLUSION: a manifest entry naming no registered test. Point
the runner at this one with `--expected-failures
tools/wasm/wasm_expected_failures_constraints.json` when the module carries
temper-constraints alone.
THIS FILE IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS A RESULT RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.
Measured 2026-08-11 with `node tools/wasm/run_wasm_tests.mjs` against the actual
`--no-default-features --features constraints-wasm-test-registry` build: 29 registered,
29 executed, 29 passed, 0 failed, 0 expected-fail, 0 other. An empty manifest is NOT a
weaker gate: with nothing excluded, every one of the 29 executable tests is load-bearing
and any regression on wasm32 turns the step red immediately.
THE ONE EXCLUDED TEST IS NOT AN EXCLUSION MADE HERE.
`ipc::tests::host_libm_symbols_actually_resolve` carries its own
`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` in ipc.rs, written by the crate before this
registry existed: it asserts that dlsym() resolves the host libm's `pow`, and
wasm32-unknown-unknown has no dynamic loader, so the function does not exist on this
target. gen_wasm_test_registry.py copies that cfg onto the registry entry, so the test is
absent rather than failing -- the same `no-dynamic-loader` fact temper-constraint-compiler
records as its own 70/69 gap (constraints::tests::host_libm_symbols_actually_resolve there
is a re-export of this exact kernel through temper-constraint-compiler's own module tree),
temper-geometry's 724/722 and temper-thermal's 145/143. Registered 30, executable 29.
--- Native comparison (R19), diffed by name not just counted --------------------
`cargo test --no-default-features --manifest-path
packages/temper-placer/temper-constraints/Cargo.toml` runs 30 lib tests, all passing --
the 29 wasm32 names above, PLUS `ipc::tests::host_libm_symbols_actually_resolve` (native
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu is not wasm32, so its own cfg does not exclude it there). It also
runs two integration-test targets that this crate's `tests/*.rs` contains
(`shared_ir_adapter.rs`: 3 tests, `shared_ir_adapter_pbt.rs`: 9 property tests) -- neither
references pyo3, so unlike temper-orchestration's, both compile and pass cleanly under
`--no-default-features` and need no `--lib` flag on native_test_args. Diffed name-for-name:
the 29 wasm32 names are an EXACT SUBSET of the 30 native lib names, all 29 pass on both
sides, 0 wasm32_only, 0 disagreement.
